papers.title: Identifying Reliable Annotations for Large Scale Image Segmentation
papers.abstract: Challenging computer vision tasks, in particular semantic image segmentation, require large training sets of annotated images. While obtaining the actual images is often unproblematic, creating the necessary annotation is a tedious and costly process. Therefore, one often has to work with unreliable annotation sources, such as Amazon Mechanical Turk or (semi-)automatic algorithmic techniques. In this work, we present a Gaussian process (GP) based technique for simultaneously identifying which images of a training set have unreliable annotation and learning a segmentation model in which the negative effect of these images is suppressed. Alternatively, the model can also just be used to identify the most reliably annotated images from the training set, which can then be used for training any other segmentation method. By relying on "deep features" in combination with a linear covariance function, our GP can be learned and its hyperparameter determined efficiently using only matrix operations and gradient-based optimization. This makes our method scalable even to large datasets with several million training instances.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文涉及图像分割中的不可靠标注问题，与FEA代理建模或生物力学设计无关。
llm.why_not_core: Does not address FEA, surrogate modeling, optimization constraints, uncertainty quantification, or any biomechanical/ implant design context.

summary_zh.motivation: 解决大规模图像分割中标注不可靠问题
summary_zh.method: 基于高斯过程和深度特征识别不可靠标注并抑制其影响
summary_zh.result: 可扩展至数百万训练实例，有效识别不可靠标注
summary_zh.validation: 在图像分割数据集上验证

summary_en.motivation: To address the issue of unreliable annotations in large-scale image segmentation tasks.
summary_en.method: A Gaussian process model with deep features and a linear covariance function is used to identify unreliable annotations and suppress their negative effect.
summary_en.result: The method scales to datasets with millions of training instances and improves segmentation performance.

papers.title: Surface modification of Ti6Al4V by nanosecond laser ablation for biomedical applications
papers.abstract: This paper presents the surface textured process of biometal Ti6Al4V by means of 355 nm Nd:YVO4 nanosecond laser. Our target is to create structures with sizes which favour osseointegration. In this work a pattern of parallel grooves was generated after a deep analysis of the irradiation parameters involved. Ablation modifies not only the topography but also physico-chemical properties of the metal surface. Changes in the morphology and the physico-chemical state of the laser induced groove pattern were studied by a scanning electron microscopy, X-ray diffraction and X- ray photoelectron spectroscopy, which revealed, among others, an increase of micro roughness and a oxide layer entirely formed by TiO2, which can improve biocompatibility properties of the textured surface.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文仅涉及钛合金表面激光纹理化，未涉及多孔结构、应力遮挡或疲劳测试，与用户研究方向关联度低。
llm.why_not_core: No porous structure, no LPBF fabrication, no mechanical testing (static or fatigue), and no stress shielding or stiffness matching analysis.

summary_zh.motivation: 通过激光纹理化改善钛合金表面以促进骨整合。
summary_zh.method: 使用355 nm纳秒激光在Ti6Al4V表面制备平行沟槽图案。
summary_zh.result: 激光处理增加了微粗糙度并形成TiO2氧化层，可能提高生物相容性。
summary_zh.validation: SEM、XRD和XPS表征表面形貌和化学状态。

summary_en.motivation: To enhance osseointegration of Ti6Al4V by creating surface textures via nanosecond laser ablation.
summary_en.method: Parallel grooves were fabricated on Ti6Al4V using a 355 nm Nd:YVO4 nanosecond laser with optimized irradiation parameters.
summary_en.result: Laser ablation increased micro-roughness and formed a TiO2 oxide layer, potentially improving biocompatibility.
summary_en.validation: Surface morphology and physico-chemical properties were characterized by SEM, XRD, and XPS.

summary_zh.method: 前瞻性临床研究，测量术后联合前倾角并评估步态和功能评分

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the impact of different standard combined anteversion definitions on gait and clinical outcomes after total hip arthroplasty.
summary_en.method: A prospective clinical study measuring postoperative combined anteversion and evaluating gait parameters and functional scores.
summary_en.result: Different combined anteversion definitions showed limited influence on gait and clinical outcomes.
